key_findings.title: FUN_0058CCA0 default DOES route to FUN_004D8860 - confirmed
key_findings.summary: The PATTERNDSUBD-F3 finding is fully confirmed by decomp inspection. The default branches of BOTH halves of FUN_0058CCA0's main switch (low half opcodes 0xF..0x134, high half 0x135..0x1A7) reach the shared label `switchD_0058cd4e_caseD_10` whose body is `FUN_004D8860(packet)`. This is the tier-2 to tier-3 fall-through link in the Pattern D dispatch chain (Receiver.vtable[1] -> FUN_0058CCA0 -> FUN_004D8860). The filter switch also exits via the same chain for unwhitelisted opcodes.

key_findings.title: FUN_0058CCA0 reaches 15 LuaActorImpl::vftable slots (67-81), complementing FUN_004D8860's coverage
key_findings.summary: 13 Pattern A trampolines in FUN_0058CCA0 reach LuaActorImpl::vftable slots 67-81 (Chocobo/ChocoboGrade/Goobbue/VehicleGrade/GrandCompany/null-stubs/AchievementPoint/Title/Id/AchievedCount/JobQuestCompleteTriple/JobChange/EntrustItem). This characterizes Pattern D's role as a 2-tier opcode-to-vtable-slot mapper across the actor's stateful-Receiver surface.

key_findings.title: Pattern A vs Pattern C ratio inverts vs FUN_004D8860
key_findings.summary: FUN_004D8860 was 23 Pattern A : 1 Pattern C (96% trampolines). FUN_0058CCA0 is 13 Pattern A : 24 Pattern C (35% trampolines). The Pattern C cases are the LOW opcodes (0xF, 0xCE-E5, 0xD0-DA, etc - actor-action/state-update cluster) while Pattern A dominates the HIGH opcodes (0x194-0x1A5 = mount/achievement/grandcompany cluster). key_findings.title: Filter switch + main switch redundancy reveals 2-phase dispatch
key_findings.summary: When FUN_004D8830() returns 0, opcodes outside the whitelist {0xF, 0xCC, 0xCE-conditional, 0xE2, 0xE3, 0x134, 0x137, 0x144, 0x145, 0x197, 0x1A0} return EARLY (skipping the main switch entirely). When FUN_004D8830() returns non-0, ALL opcodes proceed to the main switch. This double-checking suggests: FUN_004D8830 likely returns whether the actor is in 'safe state' (analogous to FUN_00574AA0/vtable[2]); the whitelist is the small subset of state-bootstrap opcodes that must be processed even in safe-state. This mirrors FUN_004D8860's similar entry-guard pattern (BCS-Y-0559 EventFamilyDispatcher_EntryGuardHelper_FUN_00574AA0).

key_findings.title: 0xCC and 0x137 are 'invisible cases' - filter-whitelisted but no main-switch body
key_findings.summary: Opcodes 0xCC and 0x137 are explicitly listed in the filter switch's whitelist BUT have NO corresponding case in the main switch - they always fall to the default (FUN_004D8860). This is the only mechanism by which they reach FUN_004D8860 from FUN_0058CCA0 (since the alternative is filter-rejection early return). Effectively, FUN_0058CCA0 acts as a route-validator for 0xCC/0x137 - it allows them to proceed only when the entry guard succeeds, AND only to chain into FUN_004D8860 where their actual bespoke handlers live (BCS-Y-0535/BCS-Y-0560 for 0xCC; BCS-Y-0544 for 0x137). The whitelist mechanism thus encodes 'allowed to chain' semantics distinct from 'has bespoke handler'.

key_findings.title: 0x197/0x1A0 mount-mounting paired structure

The this+0xf0 check (already in primary-state 0xf = 'mounted'?) prevents double-mounting. The differing this+0x26a value (0 for chocobo, 1 for goobbue) is a mount-type discriminator. Vehicle-grade (0x1A1 via slot 70) does NOT have this gated structure - it's a pure trampoline; suggesting 0x1A1 is a mount-property update rather than a mount-on event.

key_findings.title: Battle-result parser family 0x139/0x13A/0x13B/0x13C - 4-way sibling pattern
key_findings.summary: Cases 0x139/0x13A/0x13C all have isomorphic 85-byte wrappers (FUN_0058C880/FUN_0058C930/FUN_0058C7D0) with the exact same shape: FUN_00585800(6, packet[0x14]) [allocator], FUN_005873xx OR 0058C880 OR 00587210 [parser], FUN_005901D0 [cleanup]. They differ only in which battle-result parser they invoke. Case 0x13B uses FUN_0058C990 (cataloged BCS-Y-0416 CommandResultX18QueueWrapper) - same shape. This is the CommandResultXNN packet family. The 4-way pattern shows the dispatcher distinguishes pre-parser allocation by opcode but routes to a common cleanup.

key_findings.title: 0x177/0x179 share staging+stream pattern - 1-element vs 20-element variants
key_findings.summary: Cases 0x177 (SetActorStatus) and 0x179 (SetActorStatusAll) share the same handler chain: FUN_0058EAF0 (clear mask + 20 ushort slots), FUN_0058EAB0 (set one slot N + mask bit), FUN_00588D20 (stream-forward set bits via FUN_005752A0(i, val) vtable). 0x177 calls EAB0 once (single status), 0x179 calls EAB0 20 times in a loop. The downstream is identical. The receiver path is per data_dependency_catalog s2c_0x0179 ChangeActorSubStatStatusReceiver (FUN_008A34D0 apply, BCS-Y-0389) - so the third-router stages into a per-actor status array, then FUN_005752A0 forwards to a vtable-stored handler that pushes each set element to the receiver.

open_questions: Which Receiver class owns FUN_0058CCA0 as its vtable[1] apply method? The function has 0 instruction-level callers per Ghidra - reached only via data-pointer dispatch. The pattern-d-subdispatcher pass framed this as a tier-2 Receiver in the Pattern D chain. Resolving the parent class requires scanning .rdata/.data for pointer values matching 0x0058CCA0 (similar workflow to the lobby dispatcher table searches). Worth a dedicated future phase since it would identify the s2c packet route entry point for this entire opcode subtree.

What is FUN_0058B2A0's full case table? (sub-dispatcher at 0xCE) The 20-way fallthrough to FUN_0058ADC0 for sub-opcodes 1..0x18 suggests an action/animation cluster Decomp FUN_0058B2A0 + FUN_0058ADC0 to enumerate.

How does FUN_0058CCA0's filter switch interact with FUN_004D8860's own entry guard FUN_00574AA0? Both functions are sibling event-family dispatchers (per BCS-Y-0559 the predicate cluster includes FUN_004d8830, FUN_004d87f0, FUN_004daf00 sharing FUN_00574aa0). If FUN_004D8830 is also vtable[2] of LuaActorImpl (return_true predicate per BCS-Y-0092), then the filter switch's behavior is identical to FUN_004D8860's - meaning both tier-2 dispatchers gate identically before fanning out. Worth verifying.

0x19A SetCompletedAchievements / 0x19B SetLatestAchievements route to slot 72/73 which BCS-Y-0092 categorizes as null-stubs. Per data_dependency_catalog these packets DO contain real schemas (128-byte achievement bitset for 0x19A). Either: (a) the achievement-state mutation happens INSIDE the trampoline body via a parent virtual call (not visible in this dispatcher), (b) BCS-Y-0092's null-stub classification for slots 72/73 is incomplete and they're actually delegated to subclasses, or (c) achievement state is intentionally not reflected in client memory in 1.x. Worth re-decomping FUN_0075A490/FUN_0075A4A0 to verify.

FUN_004D8830 itself is uncataloged. The pattern-d-subdispatcher pass noted it as the entry guard predicate shared with the FUN_00574AA0 sibling cluster but did not propose a BCS-Y entry. Should be added to maintain catalog completeness for the dispatcher's entry guard contract.

0xDB sentinel check (0xc0000000) matches the engine-managed-actor-class sentinel from BCS-Y-0533 - is the case 0xDB packet referencing actor class IDs in the 0xC0000000 family (which would be dropped silently)? This connection between the dispatcher's data validation and the actor-factory-drill pass's actor-factory class ID structure is suggestive of a unified actor-id namespace check.
